name: Beckett Zhou
title: Assistant Professor
units: Daniel Guggenheim School of Aerospace Engineering
research: Professor Zhou’s research is centered on computational aerodynamics and aeroacoustics with a focus on understanding flow physics and noise generation mechanisms, as well as innovative methods for flow and noise control. Professor Zhou’s research actively involves graduate and undergraduate students, fostering the development of numerical methodologies to investigate fundamental and applied problems in aerodynamics and aeroacoustics.

name: Ming-fai Fong
title: Assistant Professor
units: Institute for Neuroscience, Neurotechnology, and Society
Wallace H. Coulter Department of Biomedical Engineering
research: The Fong Lab seeks to understand how activity and experience shape neural circuits, and to develop plasticity-based interventions for treating neurological disorders. Toward this goal, we use a variety of approaches including electrophysiology, optogenetics, behavior, computational modeling, and control systems engineering. Current work focuses on disability, rehabilitation, and learning in the central visual system.

name: Shaolan Li
title: Assistant Professor
units: School of Electrical and Computer Engineering
research: Professor Li’s research focuses on signal processing and information theory, including machine learning, data analytics, and communication systems. She develops algorithms and mathematical frameworks that enhance data interpretation and transmission efficiency. Her research involves both graduate and undergraduate students in theoretical and applied projects.

name: Zhi Jackie Yao
title: Assistant Professor
units: School of Electrical and Computer Engineering
research: Her work combines electromagnetics, ferroic materials, microelectronic devices, and high-performance multiphysics computing. She has developed multiferroic RF devices, open-source simulation tools, and co-design methods that connect material behavior to device and system performance. Her research at Georgia Tech focuses on programmable wave-material systems for communications, sensing, and computing.
